idea-plugin.name: VerifyLens
idea-plugin.description:
See per requirement whether an AI-generated change is verified, different, or not yet verified, before you commit.

AI tools say "Done, all requirements implemented." VerifyLens checks that claim against your working tree and the tests that actually ran, and shows the result in a tool window and next to the code line that decides each requirement, for example ← R2 · Different · acts on attempt 6 (requirement: 5) · but the test passes.

The tests can all pass and the requirement can still be unmet: when the AI writes the code and the test with the same misunderstanding. VerifyLens computes when a numeric condition fires, so it catches that case too.

  • No LLM, and your code never leaves your machine. Static analysis + git + your JUnit test results, all local. No telemetry.
  • Unknown stays unknown. No test or an unresolved call means "not verified", never "looks fine".
  • Same engine as the VS Code extension, so both editors give the same verdict.

Preview. Analyzes TypeScript and JavaScript. Needs Node.js 18+ and git on this machine. The UI is in English or Korean and follows the IDE language (Tools | VerifyLens | Language… changes it).

AI가 「완료」라고 한 변경이 요구사항마다 확인됨 · 다름 · 미확인인지, 커밋하기 전에 에디터에서 보여 줍니다. AI 판정 없이 코드 분석과 실제로 돌린 테스트 결과만 쓰고, 코드는 PC 밖으로 나가지 않습니다.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.9.0: a check in a function for another feature is no longer evidence (a newsletter's email check does not verify "sign-up rejects an invalid email"). A schema field taken without a check (email: z.string()) keeps a rejection rule unverified and shows the line. "Only once" needs a test that does it twice. "Even if pressed twice" is read as a scene, not a limit of two. Coupon amounts (FLAT_COUPON = 5000) are read as settings.

0.8.0: a line that only shares a number or a unit with the requirement (a string length, a list length, LOCK_MINUTES in another file, a sign-up form's age) is no longer used as evidence. A fraction is no longer within one of a whole percent (0.02 was Verified against 1%). Counting first and then rejecting allows the limit. "Once every 30 days" means 30 days must pass. Settings with a generic name (maxAge) are linked through the statement that sets them.

0.7.0: reads "are not accepted" as a refusal, "once per person" as a uniqueness check, rates stored as fractions (0.1 = 10%) and timer values (setInterval). A setting named for another thing (RETURN_FEE for a shipping fee) is no longer used as evidence.

0.6.0: time rules are read better: a time difference with no name (Date.now() - sentAt), "14 days after", "1 hour before", "1 minute window", and "blocked when it is 0".

0.5.0: says why a requirement is unverified (wording, edge value, execution order, no deciding check, no test …) and what to do next. Sign-up rules are read better: a required check must exist, "only once" is not a count, "6 digits" means exactly 6. A second setting with the same name and another value keeps the result unverified.

0.4.1: first version for JetBrains Marketplace. Adds the plugin icon. The analysis is the same as 0.4.0.

0.4.0: reads range wording such as "up to and including", "must not exceed", "3 to 20" and "1~10", and judges more requirements without keywords.
